content.text:
根据提供的源码和测试代码，**mitt 的 `on` 方法不会将事件名统一转成小写**。

**依据如下：**

1.  **实现逻辑（`src/index.ts` 第 66-73 行）**：
    `on` 方法直接通过 `all!.get(type)` 和 `all!.set(type, ...)` 操作内部的 Map 对象。它直接使用传入的 `type` 参数作为键，没有任何对字符串进行 `.toLowerCase()` 或其他大小写转换的操作。

2.  **测试验证（`test/index_test.ts` 第 79-90 行）**：
    测试名为 `'should NOT normalize case'`（不应规范化大小写），其断言明确验证了这一点：
    *   注册了 `'FOO'` 和 `'Bar'` 等事件。
    *   断言 `expect(events.get('FOO'))` 存在，但 `expect(events.has('foo'))` 为 `false`。
    *   断言 `expect(events.get('Bar'))` 存在，但 `expect(events.has('bar'))` 为 `false`。
    *   这证明事件名是**原样存储**的，不会进行大小写归一化。

**结论**：
`mitt` 的事件名是区分大小写的，注册时传入什么字符串，内部 Map 中就存储什么字符串，不会自动转换为小写。

# Mitt

> Tiny 200b functional event emitter / pubsub.

-   **Microscopic:** weighs less than 200 bytes gzipped
-   **Useful:** a wildcard `"*"` event type listens to all events
-   **Familiar:** same names & ideas as [Node's EventEmitter](https://nodejs.org/api/events.html#events_class_eventemitter)
-   **Functional:** methods don't rely on `this`
-   **Great Name:** somehow [mitt](https://npm.im/mitt) wasn't taken

Mitt was made for the browser, but works in any JavaScript runtime. It has no dependencies and supports IE9+.

### mitt

Mitt: Tiny (~200b) functional event emitter / pubsub.

Returns **Mitt**

  "name": "mitt",
  "version": "3.0.1",
  "description": "Tiny 200b functional Event Emitter / pubsub.",
  "module": "dist/mitt.mjs",

  "jsnext:main": "dist/mitt.mjs",
  "umd:main": "dist/mitt.umd.js",

    "types": "./index.d.ts",
    "module": "./dist/mitt.mjs",

    "require": "./dist/mitt.js",
    "default": "./dist/mitt.mjs"
  },
  "scripts": {
    "test": "npm-run-all --silent typecheck lint mocha test-types",
    "mocha": "mocha test",
    "test-types": "tsc test/test-types-compilation.ts --noEmit --strict",
    "lint": "eslint src test --ext ts --ext js",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",

// An event handler can take an optional event argument
// and should not return a value

## Install

This project uses [node](http://nodejs.org) and [npm](https://npmjs.com). Go check them out if you don't have them locally installed.

```sh
$ npm install --save mitt
```

Then with a module bundler like [rollup](http://rollupjs.org/) or [webpack](https://webpack.js.org/), use as you would anything else:

```javascript
// using ES6 modules
import mitt from 'mitt'

// using CommonJS modules
var mitt = require('mitt')
```

The [UMD](https://github.com/umdjs/umd) build is also available on [unpkg](https://unpkg.com):

```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/mitt/dist/mitt.umd.js"></script>
```

You can find the library on `window.mitt`.
